passage:
A museum displayed a flute made from bone. It was thousands of years old.
Students were amazed that people so long ago made music. They had imagined ancient life as only hunting, farming, and survival.
The guide said music may have helped people tell stories, comfort children, mark ceremonies, or simply enjoy sound.
A musician played a modern copy of the flute. The sound was thin but beautiful.
The students stood quietly. For a moment, the distance between past and present felt smaller.
The flute showed that art is not a luxury that appears after life becomes easy. It is part of being human.
